functions.name: Govern
functions.blurb: Risk strategy, roles, policy, oversight and supply-chain risk. New in CSF 2.0 — the function that makes the rest accountable.

functions.name: Identify
functions.blurb: Know your assets, data flows, threats and weaknesses. You cannot defend what you cannot enumerate.

functions.name: Protect
functions.blurb: Safeguards that prevent or limit impact: identity, data security, platform hardening, resilient infrastructure.

functions.name: Detect
functions.blurb: Continuous monitoring and adverse-event analysis so compromise is found in minutes, not months.

functions.name: Respond
functions.blurb: Incident management, analysis, communication and mitigation once a detection is declared an incident.

functions.name: Recover
functions.blurb: Restore assets and operations, verify integrity, and communicate recovery.

properties.name: Authentication
properties.blurb: Spoofing — pretending to be someone or something else. Countered by strong authentication.

properties.name: Integrity
properties.blurb: Tampering — modifying data, code or configuration without authority. Countered by integrity controls.

properties.name: Non-repudiation
properties.blurb: Repudiation — denying an action because nobody can prove it. Countered by trustworthy audit trails.

properties.name: Confidentiality
properties.blurb: Information disclosure — exposing data to those not authorised to see it. Countered by encryption and access control.

properties.name: Availability
properties.blurb: Denial of service — degrading or denying legitimate use. Countered by capacity, redundancy and recovery.

properties.name: Authorisation
properties.blurb: Elevation of privilege — gaining capabilities without authorisation. Countered by least privilege and separation of duties.

govern.spoofing.name: Identity & Access Policy
govern.spoofing.flavour: Who may be who, and how we prove it
govern.spoofing.desc: Board-endorsed policy that sets identity assurance levels, MFA expectations and account lifecycle rules. Without it, authentication controls are optional in practice.

govern.tampering.name: Change Management Board
govern.tampering.flavour: Nothing ships without a name on it
govern.tampering.desc: Formal change control: approvals, separation between requester and deployer, and rollback plans. Unauthorised change is Tampering by another name.

govern.repudiation.name: Logging & Retention Standard
govern.repudiation.flavour: If it is not logged it did not happen
govern.repudiation.desc: Defines what must be logged, for how long, and who may delete it. Sets the evidentiary baseline for every investigation and regulator question.

govern.disclosure.name: Data Classification Policy
govern.disclosure.flavour: Label it before you lose it
govern.disclosure.desc: A classification scheme with handling rules per tier. Drives encryption, access and DLP decisions and decides what a breach actually costs.

govern.dos.name: Resilience & Impact Tolerance
govern.dos.flavour: How long can we be down? Write it down
govern.dos.desc: Board-set maximum tolerable downtime for critical services, funded and tested. Turns “availability” from a wish into a requirement.

govern.elevation.name: Separation of Duties
govern.elevation.flavour: No one person holds every key
govern.elevation.desc: Policy that splits request, approve and execute for sensitive actions. Limits what a single stolen or malicious privileged account can do.

identify.spoofing.name: Identity Inventory
identify.spoofing.flavour: Humans, services, keys, bots — all of them
identify.spoofing.desc: A complete inventory of human, service and machine identities and their owners. Orphaned service accounts are a favourite foothold.

identify.tampering.name: Software Bill of Materials
identify.tampering.flavour: Know what is inside the box
identify.tampering.desc: SBOMs and provenance records for software and firmware so a poisoned component can be found and scoped in hours.

identify.repudiation.name: Log Source Inventory
identify.repudiation.desc: An inventory of what generates telemetry, what is collected and what is silent. Gaps here become “we cannot tell what happened”.

identify.disclosure.name: Data Flow Mapping
identify.disclosure.flavour: Where does the sensitive stuff actually go?
identify.disclosure.desc: Diagrams and discovery tooling showing where sensitive data is stored, processed and transmitted. The raw material of every threat model.

identify.dos.name: Critical Dependency Map
identify.dos.flavour: The thing the thing depends on
identify.dos.desc: Maps the services, suppliers and utilities each critical function needs — including the boring ones like DNS, power and the one SaaS nobody remembers.

identify.elevation.name: Attack Path Mapping
identify.elevation.flavour: See the route to Domain Admin first
identify.elevation.desc: Graph-based analysis of privilege relationships and attack paths, plus authenticated vulnerability scanning, so the shortest path to crown jewels is closed before an attacker walks it.

protect.spoofing.name: Phishing-Resistant MFA
protect.spoofing.flavour: FIDO2 beats a lookalike login page
protect.spoofing.desc: Hardware-bound, origin-checked authenticators (FIDO2/passkeys) that cannot be replayed by an adversary-in-the-middle. The single highest-value identity control.

protect.tampering.name: Code Signing & Integrity Checks
protect.tampering.flavour: Trust the signature, not the filename
protect.tampering.desc: Cryptographic signing of code, firmware and configuration, verified at install and boot. Stops unauthorised modification being silently accepted.

protect.repudiation.name: Tamper-Evident Audit Logging
protect.repudiation.flavour: Logs the intruder cannot quietly edit
protect.repudiation.desc: Logs shipped off-host to append-only storage with integrity protection, so an intruder with local admin cannot erase their trail.

protect.disclosure.name: Encryption In Transit & At Rest
protect.disclosure.flavour: Make a stolen disk a boring disk
protect.disclosure.desc: TLS everywhere and strong at-rest encryption with managed keys. Turns many data-theft events into non-events.

protect.dos.name: Rate Limiting & DDoS Shield
protect.dos.flavour: Absorb the flood, serve the humans
protect.dos.desc: Upstream scrubbing, rate limits, autoscaling and sane timeouts so volumetric and application-layer floods degrade gracefully.

protect.elevation.name: Least Privilege & PAM
protect.elevation.flavour: Admin rights are a loan, not a gift
protect.elevation.desc: Role-based access with just-in-time elevation, vaulted privileged credentials and no standing admin. Limits blast radius when any one account falls.

detect.spoofing.name: Identity Threat Detection
detect.spoofing.desc: Behavioural analytics on sign-ins and sessions: impossible travel, token replay, MFA fatigue patterns and anomalous consent grants.

detect.tampering.name: File Integrity Monitoring
detect.tampering.flavour: Tell me when the binary changes
detect.tampering.desc: Baseline hashes and alerts on unexpected changes to critical files, configs and firmware. Catches implants and web shells.

detect.repudiation.name: SIEM Correlation
detect.repudiation.flavour: One alert is noise, five is a story
detect.repudiation.desc: Correlates events across sources to turn scattered log lines into a timeline. The heart of a SOC.

detect.disclosure.name: DLP & Egress Anomaly Detection
detect.disclosure.flavour: Why is the file server talking to Moldova?
detect.disclosure.desc: Content-aware and volumetric detection of data leaving the environment, including slow-drip exfiltration over allowed channels.

detect.dos.name: Saturation & Health Monitoring
detect.dos.desc: Capacity, latency and error-budget monitoring that spots degradation before customers do and separates attack from success.

detect.elevation.name: Privilege Escalation Analytics
detect.elevation.flavour: Why did svc-backup become Domain Admin?
detect.elevation.desc: Alerts on privilege grants, group changes, token manipulation and use of privileged functions outside change windows.

respond.spoofing.name: Credential Revocation & Session Kill
respond.spoofing.desc: Rapid, rehearsed ability to revoke sessions, tokens, API keys and passwords for suspected-compromised identities across every system.

respond.tampering.name: Host Isolation & Quarantine
respond.tampering.flavour: Pull the cable, keep the evidence
respond.tampering.desc: EDR-driven network containment of compromised hosts that preserves memory and disk state for analysis.

respond.repudiation.name: Forensic Evidence Preservation
respond.repudiation.flavour: Chain of custody or it never happened
respond.repudiation.desc: Collect and protect volatile and persistent evidence with integrity guarantees so findings stand up to regulators, insurers and courts.

respond.disclosure.name: Breach Notification Playbook
respond.disclosure.desc: Pre-agreed decision tree, drafts and contacts for regulator, customer and partner notification. Legal duties start at awareness, not at root cause.

respond.dos.name: Traffic Scrubbing & Failover
respond.dos.flavour: Shift the load before the pager melts
respond.dos.desc: Runbooks to activate scrubbing, traffic diversion and failover regions during a sustained attack.

respond.elevation.name: Emergency Privilege Revocation
respond.elevation.flavour: Break glass, then break their access
respond.elevation.desc: Break-glass procedures to strip standing and delegated privilege, rotate privileged secrets and lock down admin tiers mid-incident.

recover.spoofing.name: Identity Rebuild & Re-proofing
recover.spoofing.desc: Re-issue credentials and re-verify identities after compromise, including help-desk procedures resistant to social engineering.

recover.tampering.name: Golden Image Rebuild
recover.tampering.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-good, signed images and verified config rather than trusting a “cleaned” host.

recover.repudiation.name: Post-Incident Review
recover.repudiation.desc: Structured lessons-learned that feed back into detections, playbooks and risk register. Closes the loop to Govern.

recover.disclosure.name: Secret & Key Rotation
recover.disclosure.flavour: Assume every key in memory is burned
recover.disclosure.desc: Fast, automated rotation of keys, certificates and secrets that may have been exposed, with revocation of the old material.

recover.dos.name: Immutable Backups & Tested Restore
recover.dos.flavour: A backup you have not restored is a hope
recover.dos.desc: Offline or immutable backups with regular restoration tests against defined recovery objectives. Your answer to ransomware.

recover.elevation.name: Directory & Trust Rebuild
recover.elevation.desc: Procedures to recover the identity plane itself — forest recovery, trust re-establishment, tiered rebuild — when the attacker owned the directory.
